statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 16% while Stress remains high at 65%.
recommendation: Tail sits well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON. Stress stays high because the 30-year Treasury yield printed 5.62%, its highest since 2002, consumer confidence fell to its weakest since 2014 and crude remains near $90, none of which is an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 price path. A narrow danger window is published from 12:15Z to 15:30Z covering ADP, the GDP third estimate, the August PCE report, the cash open and Chicago PMI.
headline: Low Tail with high Stress: flat, two-sided overnight NQ range ahead of the ADP, GDP and August PCE data block
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures are trading near 30,603, down about 0.03% overnight, inside a 0.54% range of 30,571.00 to 30,737.00. The contract opened the overnight session around 30,714, drifted roughly 140 points to the 30,571 low and has since reclaimed it, so a meaningful retracement is observed rather than persistent one-way extension. E-mini S&P 500 futures are 0.15% higher at 7,743.25 inside a 0.23% range, a mild divergence that reflects semiconductor softness rather than index-level stress. The cash index closed 29 September at 30,339.33, up 0.21% inside a 0.64% daily range of 30,235.67 to 30,429.97 and off its session lows, while the S&P 500 eased 0.1% and the Dow 0.2%. VIX is 16.04, near the lower end of its recent range. Narrow ranges, observed retracement and low implied volatility are inconsistent with the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures, so Tail stays in the low band.

Stress remains high for reasons outside current Nasdaq-100 structure. The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.62%, its highest since 2002, and the 10-year rose about 4 basis points to 5.28%, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 4.92% at the 2-year point as of 28 September. The Conference Board consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points to 81.9, its weakest since 2014, with the present-situation component turning negative for the first time since September 2024. WTI is near $89.70 and Brent near $96.62, easing on improved Middle East supply but still elevated. Semiconductors were pressured on 29 September by AI-safety concerns tied to a leaked Anthropic listing document. Under this contract that combination of high long-end yields, weak sentiment and an elevated oil premium is a difficult but mean-reverting environment, which is Stress rather than Tail.

Two scheduled items shape the next 24 hours. The data block at 12:15Z and 12:30Z carries ADP employment, the Q2 GDP third estimate and the August PCE price index, with the 13:30Z cash open and the 13:45Z Chicago PMI immediately after, and the forecast lifts Tail into the watch band across 12:00Z to 14:00Z for that overlap. Micron reports fiscal Q4 results after the 20:00Z close against consensus near $50.9 billion in revenue, a memory and AI-memory bellwether whose stock has risen over 250% in 2026, so the forecast also lifts Tail into the watch band for the 21:00Z and 22:00Z post-close futures hours. The 1 October funding cliff has been removed: Congress passed a stopgap through 11 December, so September payrolls on 2 October are expected to be published on schedule. Shared Finviz context was not used as evidence for this assessment because the available file was roughly four hours old and reported partial collection with its calendar and futures sections unavailable; all levels above come from independent current sources.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the published Claude Tail score fell from the 23-24 watch band during the European morning of 29 September to 16 overnight, with a single 24 print at 15:00Z as the US session turned lower before closing off its lows. The score has held at 16 for the last three published hours as futures traded an orderly two-sided range. Stress decayed steadily from 79 to 65 as the oil premium eased and the 1 October funding deadline was resolved by a stopgap, while staying in the high band throughout on long-end yields and weak consumer sentiment. Confidence held between 87 and 88. No Claude assessment was published in the 14:00Z clock-hour, which remains explicitly unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band through the remaining Asian and European hours on the observed two-sided overnight range, then lifts it into the 21-23 watch band from 12:00Z to 14:00Z for the ADP, GDP and August PCE block, the 13:30Z cash open and the 13:45Z Chicago PMI. Tail eases back below the watch threshold through the US afternoon on the assumption that price discovery is orderly and retracements occur, then rises again to 20-21 for the 21:00Z and 22:00Z hours covering the post-close reaction to Micron's fiscal Q4 report in thin futures liquidity. The path returns to a 16-17 Asian baseline into 1 October. Stress remains in the high band across every hour because the yield, oil and sentiment backdrop is structural, and Confidence decays from 87 to 82 as the verified evidence underpinning this assessment ages. Every non-current hour is conditional; no future price-path structure is asserted as observed.
